bull.b: Rapid top-line expansion with gross margin near 40% signals early product-market fit and scalable revenue streams. Sustained higher gross margins provide a structural path to operating leverage as licensing and exchange volumes scale, improving the odds of eventual profitability if SG&A and R&D growth normalizes.

Meaningful available funding and a non-dilutive term sheet materially reduce near-term refinancing risk and provide runway to execute infrastructure rollouts (SanQtum) and close integrations. Durable access to capital supports conversion of backlog into revenue without immediate forced asset sales or distress financing.

bull.t: Large tokenization backlog and ecosystem partnerships
bull.b: A sizeable contract backlog plus blue-chip partnerships create durable demand visibility and distribution channels. Combined with acquisitions that expand exchange and cybersecurity capabilities, this establishes a multi-pronged revenue model (licensing, tokenization, exchange) and network effects that strengthen competitive positioning over months.

bear.b: Severe negative operating and net margins indicate the current cost base far outstrips revenue, limiting return on capital and the company's ability to self-fund growth. Persistently deep losses erode shareholder equity over time and require either sustained margin improvement or ongoing external financing to maintain operations.

bear.t: Persistent cash burn and weak cash generation
bear.b: Material negative operating and free cash flow show the business remains cash-consuming, creating dependency on capital markets or asset sales. Even with improving FCF trends, continued burn constrains strategic optionality, raises dilution risk if funding lapses, and places a premium on converting receivables and backlog into timely cash.

bear.t: High dilution and financing / governance risk
bear.b: A large, conditional structured financing that can dilute >50% and confer board/control rights poses lasting shareholder dilution and governance risks. Combined with recent share issuances and warrants, this can materially change ownership incentives, restrict strategic flexibility, and impair long-term value per share absent clear, accretive execution.
